plugins.none: No plugins of your own yet
plugins.none.description: Cast one above, or install one a colleague sent you.
plugins.builtin.description: What wisp is made of. Switching one off frees everything it made; what needs it says why
plugins.install.hint: A plugin folder a colleague sent, or its git URL (https or git@). It comes in off: you see what it asks for first.
plugins.asksNothing: It asks for nothing beyond showing itself.
plugins.cast.hint: Ask for a change to wisp. An agent writes it as a plugin; you switch it on and keep it.
plugins.cast.placeholder: A floating button that opens all my PRs…
plugins.cast.pin: Writes a plugin, not your code
plugins.cast.started: Casting: the agent writes the plugin, then you switch it on
plugins.example.1: A floating button that opens all my open PRs on GitHub, with how many there are
plugins.example.2: A top bar button that shows my wisp tool stats for the last 30 days
plugins.example.3: A "deploy" block agents can use to show where they deployed and whether it is healthy
plugins.example.4: Compact cards with bold titles, the PR first, no machine or project, and an Open PR button on hover
plugins.example.5: Quick replies above the follow-up box: Run the tests, Ship it, Explain why…
plugins.example.6: When a task finishes with failing tests, send it back once to fix them
plugins.example.7: A bigger monospace prompt box without the compare and team buttons
plugins.example.8: Codex tasks always run the linter before they report
plugins.foot.post: . Turning one off puts back exactly what it changed.
plugins.pane.lede: Changes to wisp itself: buttons, panels, blocks, looks and behaviour. Cast one, or install one a colleague sent.
